the alternation of two or more different forms in the life cycle of a plant or animal

A tissue graft taken from a species different from that of the recipient.

s.d: To perform a tissue graft using tissue taken from a species different from that of the recipient.
(geology) a piece of rock of different origin from the igneous rock in which it is embedded

s.d: A xenophobe.
x: So Buzz Bissinger sees fit that we give up on the ideal of Olympism and give in to xenophobics, terrorists, drug abusers, profiteers and human rights abusers?

Exhibiting or characterised by xenophobia, a fear or hatred of strangers, foreigners, or extraterrestrial life.
x: Residents of Plettenberg Bay this week launched violent xenophobic attacks on foreign Africans living in informal settlements, beating them and ransacking their houses

s.d: a brown-to-yellow mineral that is a phosphate of yttrium in crystalline form

x: Xeranthemums have silvery flower heads with purplish tubular flowers.

a mild form of ichthyosis characterized by abnormal dryness and roughness of the skin

s.d: a rare genetic condition characterized by an eruption of exposed skin occurring in childhood and photosensitivity with severe sunburn; inherited as a recessive autosomal trait in which DNA repair processes are defective so they are more likely to chromosome breaks and cancers when exposed to ultraviolet light
(uncountable) A rare genetic disorder in which DNA damaged by ultraviolet light is not repaired and the skin becomes sensitive to such light, in which a skin cancer can subsequently develop.
a mild form of ichthyosis characterized by abnormal dryness and roughness of the skin
(dated, uncountable) Xeroderma.
x: A boy, aged 9, had suffered from xerodermia since the second month of life.

a duplicator (trade mark Xerox) that copies graphic matter by the action of light on an electrically charged photoconductive insulating surface in which the latent image is developed with a resinous powder
a page printer that uses the xerographic process
forming an image by the action of light on a specially coated charged plate; the latent image is developed with powders that adhere only to electrically charged areas
